title: The North Face Tadpole 23 review: the classic small tent, and what to check on a used one
dek: A freestanding, three-pole classic with 8.84 mm poles and a big vestibule. Owners report 15 to 30 years of use, and fly coatings that fail on older units.
subject: The North Face Tadpole 23
verdict: The Tadpole 23 is a beloved, freestanding small tent: easy to pitch, strong in wind and rain, with a vestibule big enough to cook in. It's roomy for one and tight for two, with low headroom. On a used one, the fly coating and seam tape decide whether it's a keeper.
bestFor: Solo backpackers who want room for gear, or two close partners on short trips.
notFor: Two tall people, anyone who needs to sit up comfortably, or a used tent with a sticky, peeling fly.

body:
## The short version

The Tadpole 23 is one of the most familiar North Face tents: a freestanding two-person design with three 8.84 mm poles, an all-mesh inner and a big vestibule. Trailspace reviews run from 2004 to today, and the story is consistent. It's strong, simple and loved, and it's cramped for two.

## Weather

Many owners say it stays dry in heavy rain and handles wind well; one calls it bombproof. The leaks owners do report usually trace back to a poorly staked fly, an unsealed floor, or a fly whose coating has failed with age.

## Space

Owners describe it as a one-person tent with room for gear, or a two-person tent for close partners. You can sit up only near the door, and people over six feet often find it cramped. The vestibule is the standout: big enough for packs, boots and even cooking.

## Condensation

The mesh inner ventilates well, but the fly collects condensation in cold, damp weather, especially with two people breathing. Owners recommend staking the fly out wide and cracking the door.

## Buying a used Tadpole

This is the key point. Several owners report the fly turning sticky and the seam tape flaking after some years, and some say warranty claims were refused. Unfold the fly and check the inside coating before you buy. A Tadpole with a good fly and floor can last decades; one with a failing fly needs a replacement fly.

## Poles and parts

The Tadpole 23 uses **3 poles**, **8.84 mm** tubing.

Tadpole 23 poles are listed at 8.84 mm, slightly under the common 9 mm size, so compare diameter carefully when matching a loose pole.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Tadpole 23 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Tadpole%2023), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

A Tadpole 23 with sound coatings is still a great small tent for one, or two who don't mind closeness. The poles almost never wear out, the coatings do.
